trigger: Breach of security: unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information (a name with an SSN, or with a driver license or passport number, among other elements) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days only if good cause for delay is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected Florida individual by mail or email; the notice must give the date or date range, the information involved, and a contact at the firm
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - in the scenario about 301 of the 318 people in the census report live in Florida

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the firm reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years and provided to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if counsel supports it; not credible when SSNs and bank details were exported

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with the content listed in 501.171(3)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: No for the payroll scenario (about 301 Floridians); Yes if a breach reaches 500 or more Floridians (for example an ATS-wide breach of about 9,800 candidate records)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: No for the payroll scenario; Yes if more than 1,000 are notified

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request (may be extended or revoked in writing)
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the firm (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes the firm's personal information (payroll service, ATS and its AI subprocessor, screening provider, backup service) has a breach of its system
deadline: Vendor must notify the firm as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after its determination; the firm then gives the notices under (3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - register the breach contact with each vendor (POAM-012)

citation: Breach notification statutes of each state where affected individuals reside
trigger: Affected associates, staff, or candidates who live outside Florida (in the scenario about 17 former associates in 6 other states)
notify: Residents, and state regulators or consumer reporting agencies where each state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - counsel applies the law of each state where affected individuals reside, using the residence report from payroll

citation: E-Verify MOU for Employers Art. II.A.16
trigger: Suspected or confirmed loss of control of, or unauthorized access to, E-Verify personal data (case data and results, including printouts kept with Forms I-9) or E-Verify credentials
notify: DHS E-Verify by phone (888-464-4218) or email (E-Verify@dhs.gov) with the subject "Privacy Incident - Password"
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if E-Verify data or credentials are involved; not triggered by the payroll service alone

obligation: IRS notice of Form W-2 or SSN data loss (guidance)
citation: IRS guidance: Form W-2/SSN data theft information for businesses and payroll service providers
trigger: Theft of employee W-2 or SSN data
deadline: As soon as possible after the loss (the IRS may be able to protect employees from tax-related identity theft if told quickly)
notify: IRS at dataloss@irs.gov with the subject "W2 Data Loss" and contact details only (no employee personal information); Federation of Tax Administrators at statealert@taxadmin.org for state tax agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but recommended; the census report holds SSNs and pay data

trigger: Security incident affecting client information (client contacts, rates, or approver accounts)
deadline: Per contract (the largest client's agreement says "promptly")
notify: Client contacts in the client register
applies_at_this_tier: Only if client information is involved; associate-only data does not trigger most contracts

trigger: Suspected security incident, data breach, or fraudulent funds transfer
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline before hiring outside vendors
As soon as possible (supports recovery of diverted deposits and any 501.171(4)(b) delay request)
notify: FBI IC3 online report; local FBI field office

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand is received and payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held for a covered entity
deadline: No later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the firm is not a business associate (P03 G-144)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (proposed) - NOT YET IN EFFECT
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief of a covered incident; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until then

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the firm holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Kaspersky covered article identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the firm holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
